messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High-severity GPU OOMs observed during prefill on cluster infer-prod-us-west-2-3. Multiple containers restarting. Pager fired to oncall. Monitoring: https://mk.example/alerts/4891234567

alice: ack, I'm on it. seeing lots of prefill OOMs on model 'redwood-13b-v1' nodes a-3..a-6. containers repeatedly SIGKILL'd.

ben: grabbing logs now. any customer reports?

alice: quick glance, three customer requests returned 503s with "container restart" around 12:07 UTC. p95 latency spiked to 6s for other requests.

cheng: pasting recent kube logs from one of the pods:
```
Timestamp: 2025-11-03T12:06:43Z
[container] signal: killed
[runtime] eviction: GPU memory exceeded, attempted prefill 4.2GB beyond alloc, cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[container] restarting pod infer-13b-a-3-7/....
```

diana: also seeing repeated kernel messages on node gpunode-32:
```
Nov  3 12:06:42 gpunode-32 kernel: NVRM: Xid (0001:0): PID 4521: NVRM GPU at 0000:af:00.0: GPU page allocation failed
Nov  3 12:06:42 gpunode-32 kernel: Docker container killed due to OOM
```

eva: seems correlated with a sudden influx of very large prefill requests — some user payloads include long transcripts (~200k chars). Prefill size distribution shows a tail spike starting at 12:05 UTC.

alice: immediate mitigation steps I'm going to try: 1) attach temporary route limit to routes with large-context flag (max_prefill_bytes=64k), 2) enable prefill-trim for heavy requests, 3) mark the a-3..a-6 nodes as unschedulable for new prefill-heavy pods while we triage. will also notify CS for impacted customers.

ben: +1. I'll spin up two hot spare worker nodes in the cluster (smaller model pool) and shift a percentage of traffic (10%) to coldmodel fallback for heavy requests to avoid full restarts.

infra-bot: Scaling action started: provisioning node gpunode-40, gpunode-41. ETA ~3m.

cheng: doing quick grep in gateway logs for request sizes and route ids:
```
grep "prefill_size" /var/log/gateway/2025-11-03.log | sort -nr | head -n 20
# shows multiple requests > 300k bytes hitting /v1/chat/stream route-id=chat-large-context
```

alice: drafted an hourly customer notice for CS to send if needed. initial impact: 3 customers, transient 5-15 minute errors, degraded latency for others.

diana: could be KV cache growth + repeated prefill of same long prompts causing fragmentation. Are we running eviction on prefix cache?

eva: eviction is enabled but not aggressive for these routes. Suggest temporary disable of KV caching for chat-large-context. Also recommending increasing prefix eviction frequency to reduce peak GPU memory.

ben: I pushed a canary patch to route config: set max_prefill_bytes=65536, disable KV cache for chat-large-context, and route 10% traffic to coldmodel. Patching now.

alice: patch applied. monitoring shows initial drop in OOMs, but two containers still flapping — probably already in a bad state and need restart. planning controlled restart after quota drain.

infra-bot: Node provisioning complete: gpunode-40 online. Traffic shifting to coldmodel in progress.

cheng: telemetry: OOM rate dropped from 8/min to 0.7/min in the last 2 minutes. container restart rate down. good signal.

alice: re: long-term answer — we need a route-level prefill guard in the gateway and a runbook step to auto-trim prefill over 64k for requests flagged heavy. filing ticket: INF-2025-773.

ben: can someone take notes for next oncall? I'm going offline in 25m.

alice: handoff to cheng in 20. cheng, summary: GPU OOMs during prefill caused by long payload tail on chat-large-context. Mitigations applied: max_prefill_bytes=64k, KV cache disabled for route, 10% traffic to coldmodel, spun up spare nodes, cordoned nodes a-3..a-6 for new prefill pods. Monitoring shows OOM rate ~down. Customer impact: three customers saw 503s, estimated affected window 12:05–12:18 UTC.

cheng: ack, taking oncall. next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned until we've verified backlog cleared, 2) run memory leak checks on the model runtime over the next 2 hours, 3) follow-up ticket for autoscaling thresholds and prefill-rate limiting.

diana: for postmortem, let's capture: exact request ids, full dump of prefill sizes, KV cache metrics, and kernel Xid events. Also validate whether quantized kernel selection had any role.

eva: CS notified and holding on a short customer blameless note. I'll coordinate a follow-up with affected customers once we have final timeline.

alice: thanks all. leaving notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4891234567. cheng, ping me if you want a deeper handoff.

cheng: will do. closing pager for now but keeping watch on alert. :white_check_mark:
